acceptance: A shared deterministic history check rejects missing or non-ancestral commits in the active proposal, lifecycle, approval, review-series and recorded-validation continuation, identifying the offending record and commit. These commits and the selected candidate remain ancestors of the current checkout tip.

Candidate prerequisites include its sealed specification baseline, stamped remote baseline, authenticated revision-chain archive commits, prepared expected publication baseline and freshly fetched remote main. Each must exist and be ancestral to the selected candidate; candidate-owned inputs are read from that candidate rather than a later checkout.

Proposal review, completed review, validation admission, release preparation, direct publication and prepared publication refuse broken history before reviewer dispatch or publication effects. Freshly fetched remote history is checked before dependent effects, and an invalid continuation cannot silently start a replacement review series.

An intact prepared ancestor remains publishable after later descendant authorship, including newer descendant proposal and validation records. Divergent or missing history still refuses, and immutable prepared inputs, exact-source checks, destination checks, leased promotion and remote readback remain effective.

Maintainer review guidance rejects proposals to reset, rebase, force-push or amend published or recorded commits. The repair preserves historical records, unresolved findings, original execution statuses, request clocks and the existing fourteen-module review-policy inventory.

The synthetic Git wrapper directly executes real Git for ordinary local commands while retaining existing transport destination, directory identity, fetch mapping, journal and unsupported-operation checks. Leading options and argument boundaries cannot bypass those checks; production Git behavior is unchanged.

Focused history refusals have complete unchanged-test assertion-failure evidence before repair and pass afterward. Selected interaction modules execute their complete declared cases without skips or weakened assertions, including all existing publication-admission cases.

Retained before and after measurements compare identical runner and interaction command membership under equivalent runtime and resource conditions. Demonstrate the performance improvement and an interactions duration below 300 seconds without changing original request clocks, concealing overruns or substituting a reduced command for the original category.

acceptance_tests.purpose: Exercise every history-admission entrypoint using synthetic repositories, missing and divergent commits, active-chain custody and valid descendant continuation.
Preserve complete publication admission, prepared ancestor behavior, transport refusals and native runner membership and timing evidence.
Verify shipment continuation and fixed-candidate publication during later authorship, including failure and recovery behavior.
Preserve command-evidence ancestry and exact-source admission through prepared publication consumers.
Verify active review-series continuity, retained findings and custody, and rejection instead of silent replacement after orphaning.
Verify specification and revision-history ancestry, original reproduction custody and shared validation admission.
Preserve native proposal sealing, immutable revision provenance and deterministic specification consumers with the shared history guard.

selection.reason: Cross-cutting history admission affects proposal custody, validation evidence, review continuation and publication. Select the focused refusal matrix and six directly affected interaction modules; preserve earlier immutable contracts and results. Performance comparisons retain identical measured command membership and cannot claim improvement through selection reduction.
